questions.prompt: Which web font format should you ship as your primary format?
questions.explanation: WOFF2 has the best compression and is supported across modern browsers, so it's the format to ship — you rarely need others anymore.

questions.prompt: Match each font-display value to its behaviour.

pairs.right: Hide text briefly (FOIT), then swap in the web font
Show the fallback immediately, then swap (FOUT)
Use the fallback and keep it if the font is slow (best for CLS)
Very short block, short swap window, else keep the fallback

questions.explanation: block risks invisible text; swap avoids invisible text but can reflow; optional avoids the shift; fallback is a compromise between them.

questions.prompt: A font <link rel="preload"> must include the ____ attribute, or the font downloads twice.
questions.explanation: Fonts are fetched in anonymous CORS mode, so a preload without crossorigin doesn't match the real request and causes a duplicate download.

questions.prompt: Which practices reduce the performance impact of web fonts? Select all that apply.

options.text: Subset to only the glyphs you use (unicode-range)
Preload the critical font with crossorigin
Use font-display: block on all text so nothing shows until fonts load

questions.explanation: WOFF2, subsetting, and a correct preload all help. font-display: block leaves text invisible (FOIT) while fonts load, which hurts perceived speed.

questions.prompt: How can you reduce the layout shift (CLS) caused when a fallback font swaps to the web font?

options.text: Match the fallback's metrics with size-adjust/ascent-override, or use font-display: optional
Load the font with JavaScript after everything else

questions.explanation: Matching the fallback's metrics keeps line lengths and heights the same across the swap, and font-display: optional avoids the swap entirely — both cut swap-driven CLS.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to add a web font with good performance.

items.text: Choose WOFF2 and subset it to needed glyphs
Preload the critical font with crossorigin
Add a metric-matched fallback to reduce swap shift

questions.explanation: Prepare an efficient, subset WOFF2; declare it with a chosen font-display; preload the critical one (with crossorigin); and stabilize the swap with matched fallback metrics.
